# Two Emissions Tracks in the Acid Rain Program

Under Title IV’s Acid Rain Program, sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the power sector were regulated through different mechanisms. In the sulfur dioxide system, each covered allowance represents permission to emit one ton under an aggregate cap, with allowances traded among participants.

Sulfur dioxide coverage expanded in phases. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants. Substitution or compensating units brought the Phase I total to 445 units. Phase II began in 2000, and the final cap, reached in 2010, was 8.95 million tons.

The nitrogen oxides component followed a separate track. For certain coal-fired units, regulation began in 1996 and was rate-based, without a cap or allowance trading. The program therefore used distinct mechanisms and timelines for its two pollutants.
